predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: Khwarazm, a Seljuk governorship: 'Seljuk rule in Khwarazm (r.

successors.name: Khwarazmian Empire
successors.text: the shahdom of Khwarazm under Ala ad-Din Muhammad (Muhammad II), with Khorasan and western Iran

rulers.name: Qutb ad-Din Muhammad I (Arslan Tigin Muhammad)

ledger.x: 1077: Anush Tigin Gharchai becomes governor of Khwarazm.
1138: Atsiz rebels and Sanjar marches on Khwarezm.
1138: Atsiz conquers Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya.
1141: Atsiz invades Khorasan after Qatwan.
1142: Sanjar expels Atsiz from Khorasan.
1143: Sanjar subdues Khwarezm again.
1152: Qara Khitai occupy Jand.
1152: Atsiz retakes Jand in April.
1180: Sultan-Shah holds Merv against his brother Tekish.
1187: Tekish takes Nishapur.
1193: Sarakhs surrenders.
1193: Tekish takes Ray.
1193: Tekish takes Merv after Sultan-Shah's death.
1193: the rivalry with Sultan-Shah ends with Merv in Tekish's hands (December 1193).
1194: Tekish defeats and kills Tughril III at the Battle of Rayy, 4 March.
1194: the struggle for Ray ends with Tughril III's death.
1194: the Khwarazmians hold Persian Iraq, including Isfahan, by 25 June.
1195: the caliph's army retakes Persian Iraq.
1196: Tekish wins Hamadan back.
1198: Tekish besieges Herat.
1198: Tekish makes peace with the Ghurids and the caliph.
1199: Tekish crushes Mayachuq's revolt in Mazandaran.
1199: the revolt ends with Mayachuq's execution at Ardahn.
1200: the Ghurids take Khorasan after Tekish's death. the Ghurids took control of all Khorasan after Tekish died; Tekish died on 3 July 1200 and Muhammad II succeeded.
1201: the shahs pass into the 'Khwarezmid Empire' row.

wars.name: Atsiz's rebellion against Sanjar
wars.outcome: Hazarasp (1138): Sanjar wins and installs Suleiman Shah, who cannot hold the province; Atsiz returns, submits in 1141, invades Khorasan after Qatwan, is expelled in 1142 and made a vassal again in 1143; Sanjar marches again in 1147.

wars.name: Battle of Qatwan and the Qara Khitai raid on Khwarezm
wars.outcome: Qara Khitai defeat Sanjar on 9 September 1141; Khwarazm becomes their vassal and pays 30,000 dinars a year after a raid in 1142.

wars.name: Atsiz's Khorasan campaign
wars.outcome: Atsiz occupies Merv, Nishapur and Sarakhs after Qatwan and is driven out by Sanjar in 1142.

wars.name: Tekish's war with Sultan-Shah
wars.outcome: Sultan-Shah holds Merv by 1180, takes Tus (1181) and is beaten by the Ghurids at Marw al-Rudh (1190); Tekish takes Nishapur (May 1187), Sarakhs (1193) and Merv (December 1193) after Sultan-Shah's death.

wars.name: Khwarezmid conquest of Persian Iraq (Battle of Rayy)
wars.outcome: Tekish takes Ray (January 1193), kills Tughril III at Rayy (4 March 1194) and holds Persian Iraq by 25 June 1194.

wars.name: Khwarezmid-Abbasid war over Persian Iraq
wars.outcome: The caliph's army takes Hamadan, Ray and (late 1195) Isfahan; Tekish wins at Hamadan on 15 July 1196 and the town surrenders on 18 July.

wars.name: Tekish's war with the Ghurids over Herat
wars.outcome: Tekish besieges Herat from Tus in 1198 and makes peace; after his death in July 1200 the Ghurids take all Khorasan.

wars.name: Tekish's Assassin campaign
wars.outcome: Tekish captures the fortress of Qahira/Arslan-Gushay after a 4-month siege but fails at Alamut; the Isma'ilis of Turshiz agree to pay 100,000 dinars and sign a truce.

certainty.note: The oases of Khwarezm are approximate and the Syr Darya, Karakum and Khorasan frontiers are not fixed on any page; the Persian Iraq line of 1194-1199 changed hands three times (1194, late 1195, July 1196).
